newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 19.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- NEW THREAT TO COAL AS DASH FOR GAS GATHERS PACE

According to National Grid, a new 'dash for gas' is gathering momentum in the electricity market with the amount of gas-fired capacity set to double over the next three years. The Grid says that the size of the expansion is another blow to the country's biggest coal producer, RJB Mining. Data from the Grid suggests overcapacity in the generating market will continue to rise as a result.
-- FIRMS ADMIT LATE PAYMENT POLICY

According to a survey of companies by the accountancy firm Grant Thornton and the Business Strategies forecasting group, British companies pay their invoices after 49 days, 12 days faster than the average for 19 European countries. According to 54 percent of the companies surveyed, delay in the UK is intentional. Barbara Roche, Britain's small business minister, said that this is the second survey in a month which shows that Britain has one of the highest figures in Europe for intentional late payment.
-- CREST 'CAN COPE WITH HALIFAX FLOTATION'

Iain Saville, the chief executive of the Crest share settlement system, has told private client stockbrokers that he is confident the market will cope with the flotation of the Halifax. The conversion will create 7.5 million shareholders, many of whom will sell soon after. He told a conference of the Association of Private Client Investment Management and Stockbrokers that the equity market will be able to handle a bigger flotation than the one for the Alliance & Leicester.
THE TIMES
-- FORMULA ONE CHIEF AGREES ONE BLN STG PRICE CUT TO GET FLOAT OFF THE GRID

Chief executive of Formula One, Bernie Ecclestone, has agreed to cut one billion stg in the valuation of the motor racing marketing business so that it can be floated on the international stock markets. US investment bank, Salomon Brothers, is to announce a timetable for the issue, which could be as low as 1.5 billion stg. Key deals with the Formula One racing teams have yet to be finalised.
-- AMSTRAD GIVEN BOOST IN $186 MLN US LEGAL FIGHT

The chance of Amstrad winning a second court battle over allegedly faulty components supplied for its personal computers has been increased by disarray among its opponent's lawyers. Amstrad is to sue Western Digital Corp, a US disk drive manufacturer, for $186 million in the US courts. Irell & Manella, the law firm that Western has employed since 1991 to fight Amstrad has been disqualified from the case.
-- LONRHO LOOKS AT TWO BILLION STG MERGER

Lonrho has received an approach from South African mining company, JCI, regarding a two billion stg merger. Chief executive Nick Morrell has asked Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the group's merchant bank, to look at proposals. The scheme would involve Lonrho making an agreed bid for JCI of about 900 million stg, and funding this by selling its 41 percent stake in the Ghanaian mining group Ashanti to Anglo.
THE GUARDIAN
-- EXPORTERS RAP 'MYOPIC' BANK

The Bank of England has been castigated by the Institute of Export, the industry body representing exporters, for taking a 'myopic' view on interest rates. The institute says the Bank's new monetary committee should take a more 'global perspective' and the Bank's desire to cut down on inflation with an early rate rise would cause further problems for exporters. Also, there is evidence that confidence among Britain's exporters has fallen to a three-year low which places more pressure on the Bank not to raise interest rates.
-- ANGRY CO-OP CLOSES RANKS

The annual meeting of the Co-operative Wholesale Society has seen Co-op leaders promising to renew attempts to unify the movement after receiving backing from membership for their resistance to a takeover. Delegates attacked the City for backing the 1.2 billion stg takeover bid by Andrew Regan's Lanica Trust. A resolution supporting the leadership's stance was passed by more than 70,000 votes. Lennox Fife, chairman, said the resolution should deter any other predators.
-- GRANADA GOBBLES UP CATERING FIRM

Media and leisure conglomerate Granada is to unveil a 10 million stg deal to acquire Baxter & Platts, one of the UK's biggest independent contract caterers with an annual turnover of 23 million stg. The company has 130 contracts, which include Glaxo Wellcome, Whitbread and the Financial Times, and last year was named Food Service Caterer of the Year by trade magazine Caterer & Housekeeper.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- FRANCE CASTS DOUBT ON GUINNESS MERGER

French authorities are worried that the 23 billion stg merger of Guinness and Grand Met will mean the global distribution of champagne will become British controlled. The French government is preparing to lobby Brussels when they examine the proposed merger. Guinness already has an exclusive world distribution deal with Moet Hennessy, the world's biggest champagne company.
-- WELFARE STATE 'HAS REACHED CRISIS POINT'

According to Robert Skidelsky, in a paper published by the Social Market Foundation, the welfare state has been a failure and the state should stop funding anything beyond a minimum safety net. He claims that the Government should slash taxes and let people pay for their own welfare services rather than divert resources from social security to health and education. He argues that the welfare state has reached crisis because voters have become unwilling to pay taxes to fund increased spending.
-- REBEL FLORISTS REQUEST ADVICE FROM QC

The new board of directors for Interflora will receive legal advice which will determine whether they can press ahead with a review of the flower delivery organisation. The new management team claimed that written advice from a barrister should back up the decision to ignore calls for a postal ballot of members on the ousting of the previous board. David Parry, the outgoing chairman, has said he is considering legal action if the new board continues to refuse to hold a ballot.
